beats: [d:intrigue][sfx:boom][act:awe, measured]The oldest known fossils of our own species, Homo ^sapiens, weren't found in East ^Africa, where many expected them.
[d:tension][act:the reveal, a small smile][tune:fall]They came from a mine in ^Morocco, on the far side of the ^continent.

[d:calm][act:storytelling]In {1961|nineteen sixty-one}, miners at Jebel ^Irhoud found a ^skull. [act:plain, building]From {2004|two thousand four}, a team led by Jean-Jacques Hublin dug ^again, and found ^more: the remains of at least five ^people.

[d:build][act:the method, curious][tune:rise]But how ^old? [act:explaining]In the same layer lay flint tools that had been burnt in ancient ^fires. [p:0.93][act:explaining, a simple picture]Heating a flint resets a tiny clock inside it to ^zero. [act:explaining]After that, natural radiation fills it up again, slowly, like rain filling a ^bucket. [act:explaining]Measure how full it is, and you know when the fire ^burned. [p:0.9][act:the reveal, strong]About three hundred and fifteen ^thousand years ago. [act:context, wonder]More than a hundred thousand years older than the earlier record@noun, in ^Ethiopia.

[d:build][act:describing, intrigued]Now look at the ^skulls. [act:describing]The faces look ^modern, much like ^ours. [act:the twist, precise]But the braincases are long and ^archaic, not round like ^ours. [p:0.93][act:the idea, clear]Our lineage, it seems, got its face ^first, and its round head ^later.

[d:reveal][act:the new find, excited but measured]Then, in {2026|twenty twenty-six}, a second surprise: jaws and teeth from a quarry in ^Casablanca. [p:0.9][act:the big number, slowly]About seven hundred and seventy-three ^thousand years old. [act:a simple picture]More than twice the age of ^Irhoud.

[d:build][go:4|0][act:explaining, curious][tune:rise]How do you date a ^quarry? [p:0.93][act:explaining, a simple picture]Every so often, Earth's magnetic field ^flips: the compass needle would swing from north to ^south. [act:explaining]Some layers lock in the field as they form, like tiny compass needles frozen in ^place. [act:precise, delighted]Here the layers record@verb a known ^flip, and the fossils lie with it. [act:precise]Their shape places them near the ^root of our lineage.

[d:verdict][p:0.95][act:weighing it][tune:rise]North Africa, part of our species' story from the ^start? [act:the verdict, confident][tune:fall]*Strong ^evidence*. [act:fair]Whether the people of Irhoud count as fully Homo ^sapiens, with those long heads, is still debated.
[d:tension][p:0.93][act:the big picture, warm]Not one ^cradle. [act:the last word, quiet wonder][tune:fall]A whole ^continent.
